sanskrit_cite: itthameva divārātrinyūnādhikyakramaṃ vadet yathā deheṣvahorātranyūnādhikyādi no samam

plain_english: So too in cities it is declared by that distinction, by the sun of Shri Traiyambaka.
sanskrit_cite: tathā pureṣvapītyevaṃ tadviśeṣeṇa noditam śrītraiyambakasantānavitatāmbarabhāskaraḥ

plain_english: Shri Shambhu thus spread the day-night order to me; Shri Santanaguru said the place of awakened and unawakened.
sanskrit_cite: dinarātrikramaṃ me śrīśaṃbhuritthamapaprathat śrīsantānagurustvāha sthānaṃ buddhāprabuddhayoḥ

plain_english: Beginning from the heart, the night-day division by that is within the false white side, the part of entering delight.
sanskrit_cite: hṛda ārabhya yattena rātrindivavibhājanam tadasatsitapakṣe@ntaḥ praveśollāsabhāgini

plain_english: How can the unawakened place be day? Enough with this; this is not my prior opinion.
sanskrit_cite: abuddhasthānamevaitaddinatvena kathaṃ bhavet alaṃ vānena nedaṃ vā mama prāṅmatamatsaraḥ

plain_english: But shown to disciples, seers of the true path explain the dark fortnight, the moon gone to breath.
sanskrit_cite: heye tu darśite śiṣyāḥ satpathaikāntadarśinaḥ vyākhyātaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣo ya statra prāṇagataḥ śaśī

plain_english: By nourishing the self one by one, one digit is abandoned each tithi; near the twelve-end, that fifteenth drop remains.
sanskrit_cite: āpyāyanātmanaikaikāṃ kalāṃ pratitithi tyajet dvādaśāntasamīpe tu yāsau pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ

plain_english: Here at new moon the waned moon enters the breath-sun; it is said in Shri Kamika, and supreme nature, Maya, proceeds in half-halves in two-part Shiva form.
sanskrit_cite: sāmāvasyātra sa kṣīṇaścandraḥ prāṇārkamāviśet uktaṃ śrīkāmikāyāṃ ca nordhve@dhaḥ prakṛtiḥ parā ardhārdhe kramate māyā dvikhaṇḍā śivarūpiṇī

plain_english: By moon-sun self the body is filled and dissolved; nectar is by moon form, twofold and sixteenfold again.
sanskrit_cite: candrasūryātmanā dehaṃ pūrayetpravilāpayet amṛtaṃ candrarūpeṇa dvidhā ṣoḍaśadhā punaḥ

plain_english: All gods drink the ten-five supreme digits; new moon remains in the cave and nourishes the world.
sanskrit_cite: pivanti ca surāḥ sarve daśapañca parāḥ kalāḥ amā śeṣaguhāntaḥsthāmāvāsyā viśvatarpiṇī

plain_english: Thus the fifteen digits of the moon are consumed in order; the sixteenth, identical with nourishing immortal form, is not consumed.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kalāḥ pañcadaśa kṣīyante śaśinaḥ kramāt āpyāyinyamṛtābrūpatādātmyātṣoḍaśī na tu

plain_english: There the fifteen-digit portion is the tuṭi of the waned moon; its upper half is called the fortnight-juncture.
sanskrit_cite: tatra pañcadaśī yāsau tuṭiḥ prakṣīṇacandramāḥ tadūrdhvagaṃ yattuṭyardhaṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ sa kīrtitaḥ

plain_english: Therefore from rest in the half-tuti at new moon, the prior half, the supreme pratipada, and the other half — that juncture is posited.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādviśramatuṭyardhādāmāvasyaṃ purādalam paraṃ prātipadaṃ cārdhamiti saṃdhiḥ sa kalpyate

plain_english: There on pratipada, that prior half of the half-tuti being new-moon, by lunar-day-cut one performs and enters the solar eclipse.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prātipade tasmiṃstuṭyardhārdhe purādalam āmāvasyaṃ tithicchedātkuryātsūryagrahaṃ viśat

plain_english: There in the solar disc the moon, dissolved, drips its honey; once heated, the sun-companion — Simhika's son — drinks that honey.
sanskrit_cite: tatrārkamaṇḍale līnaḥ śaśī sravati yanmadhu taptatvāttatpibedindusahabhūḥ siṃhikāsutaḥ

plain_english: The sun is the measure, the moon the measurable, both knowledge-and-action-natured; Rahu the maya-observer is skilled at covering them.
sanskrit_cite: arkaḥ pramāṇaṃ somastu meyaṃ jñānakriyātmakau rāhurmāyāpramātā syāttadācchādanakovidaḥ

plain_english: From that clash, the darkness-natured one cannot melt them; from the union of the two, the primary measurer is the melter.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva tamorūpo vilāpayitumakṣamaḥ tatsaṃghaṭṭādvayollāso mukhyo mātā vilāpakaḥ

plain_english: From the clash of sun, moon and Rahu: measure, knowable and knower as non-dual — therefore this great graha is meritorious.
sanskrit_cite: arkendurāhusaṃghaṭṭāt pramāṇaṃ vedyavedakau advayena tatastena puṇya eṣa mahāgrahaḥ

plain_english: Even without new-moon this clash is a great graha — as when the sun is in Aries and Rahu in Asvini on an Asvini day.
sanskrit_cite: amāvasyāṃ vināpyeṣa saṃghaṭṭaścenmahāgrahaḥ yathārke meṣage rāhāvaśvinīsthe@śvinīdine

plain_english: When on new-moon the half is dissolved in the half of pratipada and the pratipadi is fully pure — that is liberation in the distant rite.
sanskrit_cite: āmāvāsyaṃ yadā tvardhaṃ līnaṃ prātipade dale pratipacca viśuddhā syāttanmokṣo dūrage vidhau

plain_english: Between eclipse and liberation: bathing, meditation, homa, japa and the rest — worldly and unworldly — their further fruit becomes beyond-worldly.
sanskrit_cite: grāsamokṣāntare snānadhyānahomajapādikam laukikālaukikaṃ bhūyaḥphalaṃ syātpāralaukikam

plain_english: Entering the moment of dissolution of the eclipsed and eclipsor disturbance, one performs liberation-share meditation, worship and the rest at the moon-sun eclipse.
sanskrit_cite: grāsyagrāsakatākṣobhaprakṣaye kṣaṇamāviśan mokṣabhāgdhyānapūjādi kurvaṃścandrārkayorgrahe

plain_english: Lunar-day cut brings debt, cough, increase, exhalation, wealth; effortless and effort-born signs differ by exhalation and restraint.
sanskrit_cite: tithiccheda ṛṇaṃ kāso vṛddhirniḥśvasanaṃ dhanam ayatnajaṃ yatnajaṃ tu recanādatha rodhanāt

plain_english: Thus breath enters the consciousness-sun, which fills the nectar-filled moon one by one with consciousness-rays by measure.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ prāṇe viśati citsūrya induṃ sudhāmayam ekaikadhyena bodhāṃśu kalayā paripūrayet

plain_english: These fifteen lunar days of the bright fortnight are beautiful moon-nectar days.
sanskrit_cite: kramasaṃpūraṇāśāliśaśāṅkāmṛtasundarāḥ tuṭyaḥ pañcadaśaitāḥ syustithayaḥ sitapakṣagāḥ

plain_english: At the last full lunar day there is previous fortnight junction; moon seizure occurs at first-day junction from previous entry.
sanskrit_cite: antyāyāṃ pūrṇamastuṭyāṃ pūrvavatpakṣasandhitā indugrahaśca pratipatsandhau pūrvapraveśataḥ

plain_english: Here worldly seizure gives practitioners great fruit; another month is called breath-course.
sanskrit_cite: aihikaṃ grahaṇe cātra sādhakānāṃ mahāphalam prāgvadanyadayaṃ māsaḥ prāṇacāre@bda ucyate

plain_english: Sun standing in six fingers from heart through capricorn makes the sixfold northern course.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsvaṅguleṣvarko hṛdayānmakarādiṣu tiṣṭhanmāghāḍhikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ kuryāttaccottarāyaṇam

plain_english: After three transits and eighteen fingers, when sun reaches aries, there is meritorious otherworldly equinox.
sanskrit_cite: saṃkrāntitritaye vṛtte bhukte cāṣṭādaśāṅgule meṣaṃ prāpte ravau puṇyaṃ viṣuvatpāralaukikam

plain_english: When sun enters libra, that same becomes equinox here, giving success in southern course.
sanskrit_cite: praveśe tu tulāsthe@rke tadeva viṣuvadbhavet iha siddhipradaṃ caitaddakṣiṇāyanagaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: Embryo state, desire to manifest, manifesting, future becoming, and beginning of manifestation are described.
sanskrit_cite: garbhatā prodbubhūṣiṣyadbhāvaścāthodbubhūṣutā udbhaviṣyattvamudbhūtiprārambho@pyudbhavasthitiḥ

plain_english: Birth, being, change, growth, decline, and decay occur in order from capricorn; action here produces similar fruit.
sanskrit_cite: janma sattā pariṇatirvṛddhirhrāsaḥ kṣayaḥ kramāt makarādīni tenātra kriyā sūte sadṛkphalam

plain_english: In otherworldly context, fish and pitcher from mantra etc prior service yield fourfold increasing result.
sanskrit_cite: āmutrike jhaṣaḥ kumbho mantrādeḥ pūrvasevane catuṣkaṃ kila mīnādyamantikaṃ cottarottaram

plain_english: Indeed entry there itself yields beautiful worldly action of peace and nourishment, with fruit increasingly distant in order.
sanskrit_cite: praveśe khalu tatraiva śāntipuṣṭyādisundaram karma syādaihikaṃ tacca dūradūraphalaṃ kramāt

plain_english: At the outgoing day increases; reversed, it counter-changes — in this year five tithis run per finger-width, such is the order.
sanskrit_cite: nirgame dinavṛddhiḥ syādviparīte viparyayaḥ varṣe@smiṃstithayaḥ pañca pratyaṅgulamiti kramaḥ

plain_english: There too the day-night ordinance stands as before; in the breath-year the months from Kārtika on are measured deftly.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpyahorātravidhiriti sarvaṃ hi pūrvavat prāṇīye varṣa etasminkārtikādiṣu dakṣataḥ

plain_english: Up to the Great-Father the Rudras would be, future, here at the first of twelve; in breath the year-rise is declared — now the twelve-year rise.
sanskrit_cite: pitāmahāntaṃ rudrāḥ syurdvādaśāgre@tra bhāvinaḥ prāṇe varṣodayaḥ prokto dvādaśābdodayo@dhunā

plain_english: The dark-fortnight tithis, in each single finger-width in order, within the twelve-year rise — twelve arisen, beginning with Caitra.
sanskrit_cite: kharasāstithya ekasminnekasminnaṅgule kramāt dvādaśābdodaye te ca caitrādyā dvādaśoditāḥ

plain_english: In Caitra a mantra-rise appears; joined to the palate and again at the heart, thereby the Caitra-rise stands — the mantra-rise too.
sanskrit_cite: caitre mantroditiḥ so@pi tālunyukto@dhunā punaḥ hṛdi caitroditistena tatra mantrodayo@pi hi

plain_english: Per finger-width the tithis are posited in three hundred; in the five-part finger-width the year would be, in breath, by sixty-year measure again.
sanskrit_cite: pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ tu triśate parikalpite sapañcāṃśāṅgule@bdaḥ syātprāṇe ṣaṣṭyabdatā punaḥ

plain_english: Six hundreds and twenty-one thousands — this division, arising in breath, is called the sixty-year day and night.
sanskrit_cite: śatāni ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi caikaviṃśatirityayam vibhāgaḥ prāṇagaḥ ṣaṣṭivarṣāhorātra ucyate

plain_english: Whatever division and juncture stands there among prahara, half-day, night, month, season, year and sun — that juncture is sacred for meditation and worship.
sanskrit_cite: praharāharniśāmāsaṛtvabdaraviṣaṣṭigaḥ yaśchedastatra yaḥ sandhiḥ sa puṇyo dhyānapūjane

plain_english: Thus in the breath-rise this time — single-bodied as power, world-self dwelling within — has its outer form posed.
sanskrit_cite: iti prāṇodaye yo@yaṃ kālaḥ śaktyekavigrahaḥ viśvātmāntaḥsthitastasya bāhye rūpaṃ nirūpyate

plain_english: Six breaths make a cup, sixty a tube; there the tithi by thirty makes the month, and twelve of those make the year.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭ prāṇāścaṣakasteṣāṃ ṣaṣṭirnālī ca tāstathā tithistattriṃśatā māsaste dvādaśa tu vatsaraḥ

plain_english: The year of the Fathers is a day and night, from the north-south course; by their own measure that year is called divine.
sanskrit_cite: abdaṃ pitryastvahorātra udagdakṣiṇato@yanāt pitṝṇāṃ yatsvamānena varṣaṃ taddivyamucyate

plain_english: Three hundred sixty years here are human; that, divided by twelve, yields the month-number here.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ ca triśataṃ varṣāṇāmatra mānuṣam tacca dvādaśabhirhatvā māsasaṃkhyātra labhyate

plain_english: Having destroyed that day-night reckoning by thirty, one should say it; having destroyed it again by twenty-one thousand and six hundred, one should say it.
sanskrit_cite: tāṃ punastriṃśatā hatvāhorātrakalpanā vadet hatvā tāṃ caikaviṃśatyā sahasraiḥ ṣaṭśatena ca

plain_english: There one should state the breath-count, with its sixty-year beginning; again it was said by teachers in their own commentaries beginning with the glorious Raurava.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇasaṃkhyāṃ vadettatra ṣaṣṭyādyabdodayaṃ punaḥ uktaṃ ca gurubhiḥ śrīmadrauravādisvavṛttiṣu

plain_english: The day-night of the gods is a year for humans; by three hundred and sixty, the year of men becomes a god-year.
sanskrit_cite: devānāṃ yadahorātraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ sa hāyanaḥ śatatrayeṇa ṣaṣṭyā ca nṝṇāṃ vibudhavatsaraḥ

plain_english: And in the glorious Svachanda scripture that very opinion is seen: beginning with that day-night of the ancestors, and afterwards.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre ca tadeva matamīkṣyate pitṝṇāṃ tadahorātramityupakramya pṛṣṭhataḥ

plain_english: Thus the divine day-night is indeed concluded in unity; by that, the teachers who derive it from the two statements of the glorious Svachanda.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ daivastvahorātra iti hyaikyopasaṃhṛtiḥ tena ye guravaḥ śrīmatsvacchandoktidvayāditaḥ

plain_english: They deludedly called the ancestral year a divine day, in vain; thousands of divine sun-years occur in the ages, from four onward.
sanskrit_cite: pitryaṃ varṣaṃ divyadinamūcurbhrāntā hi te mudhā divyārkābdasahasrāṇi yugeṣu caturāditaḥ

plain_english: By one each decrease, among those hundreds there are eight junctions; fourteen Manus span seventy-one four-ages.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikahānyā tāvadbhiḥ śataisteṣvaṣṭa saṃdhayaḥ caturyugaikasaptatyā manvantaste caturdaśa

plain_english: There in Brahma's hand fourteen Indras proceed in order; at the end of Brahma's day, the flame of time-fire measures a lakh yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo@hastatra cendrāḥ kramādyānti caturdaśa brahmāho@nte kālavahnerjvālā yojanalakṣiṇī

plain_english: Having burned the three worlds, by smoke it puts another three to sleep, before the hells, since the manifestation of time-fire.
sanskrit_cite: dagdhvā lokatrayaṃ dhūmāttvanyatprasvāpayettrayam nirayebhyaḥ purā kālavahnervyaktiryatastataḥ

plain_english: "The Lord is stationed below, O Ishvara"—thus is the glorious Raurava opinion: when Brahma's breath is blown away, in ashes, by sweat water.
sanskrit_cite: vibhuradhaḥsthito@pīśa iti śrīrauravaṃ matam brahmaniḥśvāsanirdhūte bhasmani svedavāriṇā

plain_english: The universe flooded by that remains until the arrival of night; at the end of that night, all beings have subtle bodies.
sanskrit_cite: tadīyenāplutaṃ viśvaṃ tiṣṭhettāvanniśāgame tasminniśāvadhau sarve pudgalāḥ sūkṣmadehagāḥ

plain_english: Impelled by fire-speed, people in the world become dissolution only; while Kushmanda, Hataka, and others play in the great abode.
sanskrit_cite: agnivegeritā loke jane syurlayakevalāḥ kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakādyāstu krīḍanti mahadālaye

plain_english: At night's end he makes creation again, begun from darkness; at the end of his own hundred years stands that ruin — the Vaiṣṇava day.
sanskrit_cite: niśākṣaye punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ kurute tāmasāditaḥ svakavarṣaśatānte@sya kṣayastadvaiṣṇavaṃ dinam

plain_english: And the night is of that measure — thus the hundreds named Viṣṇu and Rudra, in order at each one's own hundred-end, perish here with the egg's waning.
sanskrit_cite: rātriśca tāvatītyevaṃ viṣṇurudraśatābhidhāḥ kramātsvasvaśatānteṣu naśyantyatrāṇḍalopataḥ

plain_english: Thus at the ends of the unmanifest tattva from the start, a hundred years in order — the day-night division would so obtain, measured by each one's own hundred-year span.
sanskrit_cite: abādyavyaktatattvānteṣvitthaṃ varṣaśataṃ kramāt dinarātrivibhāgaḥ syāt svasvāyuḥśatamānataḥ

plain_english: By thousands of Brahmā's dissolution-joys with the rasāgni fires — among the Rudras standing in the unmanifest, day and night are each of that measure.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇaḥ pralayollāsasahasraistu rasāgnibhiḥ avyaktastheṣu rudreṣu dinaṃ rātriśca tāvatī

plain_english: Then Śrīkaṇṭha alone would be the lord directly doing dissolution; all the Rudras likewise at the root are charged with māyā's womb.
sanskrit_cite: tadā śrīkaṇṭha eva syātsākṣātsaṃhārakṛtprabhuḥ sarve rudrāstathā mūle māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaḥ

plain_english: In the one named avyakta he indeed sits with Śrīkaṇṭha of Brahmā's line, lower work withdrawn — for Brahmā is there in the lower reach of thought.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktākhye hyāviriñcācchrīkaṇṭhena sahāsate nivṛttādhaḥsthakarmā hi brahmā tatrādhare dhiyaḥ

plain_english: The knower in office is not the mere experiencer; having turned only to Śiva he would become Śiva — this intermediate laya at its end is called creation.
sanskrit_cite: na bhoktā jño@dhikāre tu vṛtta eva śivībhavet sa eṣo@vāntaralayastatkṣaye sṛṣṭirucyate

plain_english: At that day's face Śrīkaṇṭha creates again toward those perfected in Sāṃkhya, Vedas, and the rest — yet complete liberation is not of this kind.
sanskrit_cite: sāṃkhyavedādisaṃsiddhāñchrīkaṇṭhastadaharmukhe sṛjatyeva punastena na samyaṅmuktirīdṛśī

plain_english: In pradhāna the day-night born of it — a hundred years of the Lord — is Śrīkaṇṭha's lifespan, the day of those dwelling in the kañcukas.
sanskrit_cite: pradhāne yadahorātraṃ tajjaṃ varṣaśataṃ vibhoḥ śrīkaṇṭhasyāyuretacca dinaṃ kañcukavāsinām

plain_english: From that sequence Niyati, Kāla, Rāga, Vidyā, and Kalā enter one another's dissolution; their lifespan is the dense day.
sanskrit_cite: tatkramānniyatiḥ kālo rāgo vidyā kaletyamī yāntyanyonyaṃ layaṃ teṣāmāyurgāhanikaṃ dinam

plain_english: At that day's wasting the universe dissolves in māyā; in the night of that measure Gahaneśa should create again.
sanskrit_cite: taddinaprakṣaye viśvaṃ māyāyāṃ pravilīyate kṣīṇāyāṃ niśi tāvatyāṃ gahaneśaḥ sṛjetpunaḥ

plain_english: Thus the unmanifest time is struck through by ten parārdhas; māyā's night of that measure would be the dissolution — that is the one so named.
sanskrit_cite: evamavyaktakālaṃ tu parārdhairdaśabhirjahi māyāhastāvatī rātrirbhavetpralaya eṣa saḥ

plain_english: The maya-time, multiplied by half-counts and by a hundred, becomes the lordly day; sound and breath create the world.
sanskrit_cite: māyākālaṃ parārdhānāṃ guṇayitvā śatena tu aiśvaro divaso nādaḥ prāṇātmātra sṛjejjagat

plain_english: During that lordly night, breath subsides, and the universe, contained in the breath-womb, moves by the sushumna path.
sanskrit_cite: tāvatī caiśvarī rātriryatra prāṇaḥ praśāmyati prāṇagarbhasthamapyatra viśvaṃ sauṣumnavartmanā

plain_english: When breath is pacified in the brahma cavity, consciousness also remains; dissolution of this proceeds part by part, from subtle to subtler.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇe brahmavile śānte saṃvidyāpyavaśiṣyate aṃśāṃśikāto@pyetasyāḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmataro layaḥ

plain_english: Multiplying the lordly time by half-counts and by a hundred gives the sadashiva day; the night is the great dissolution.
sanskrit_cite: guṇayitvaiśvaraṃ kālaṃ parārdhānāṃ śatena tu sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ rātrirmahāpralaya eva ca

plain_english: At the end of his time, sadashiva occupies the bindu, crescent, and obstructing powers, takes the moving and still universe, and dissolves into sound.
sanskrit_cite: sadāśivaḥ svakālānte bindvardhendunirodhikāḥ ākramya nāde līyeta gṛhītvā sacarācaram

plain_english: Sound, by its end-operation, pierces the brahma cavity and suddenly goes to dissolution in the shakti principle at the end of its own time.
sanskrit_cite: nādo nādāntavṛttyā tu bhittvā brahmabilaṃ haṭhāt śaktitattve layaṃ yāti nijakālaparikṣaye

plain_english: Thus far is to be known: shakti dissolves again into the pervading principle at the end of its own time, day and night.
sanskrit_cite: etāvacchaktitattve tu vijñeyaṃ khalvaharniśam śaktiḥ svakālavilaye vyāpinyāṃ līyate punaḥ

plain_english: The pervading principle dissolves that day and night; it remains unsupported, even when shakti time is struck and unsupported.
sanskrit_cite: vyāpinyā taddivārātraṃ līyate sāpyanāśrite parārdhakoṭyā hatvāpi śaktikālamanāśrite

plain_english: At that time, day and night occur; even time multiplied by half-counts goes to dissolution in the state named equality, the samanasa state.
sanskrit_cite: dinaṃ rātriśca tatkāle parārdhaguṇite@pi ca so@pi yāti layaṃ sāmyasaṃjñe sāmanase pade

plain_english: That time, named equality, would be eternal and auspicious, made of parts; its samanasa form is equality, brahman, all-pervading.
sanskrit_cite: sa kālaḥ sāmyasaṃjñaḥ syānnityo@kalyaḥ kalātmakaḥ yattatsāmanasaṃ rūpaṃ tatsāmyaṃ brahma viśvagam

plain_english: Therefore, from samanasa time, from the measure of a blink onward, minute and so forth up to the end of half-counts is produced; this is established here.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ sāmanasātkālānnimeṣonmeṣamātrataḥ tuṭyādikaṃ parārdhāntaṃ sūte saivātra niṣṭhitam
